exclude: The fast loader that loads side A's GAME file: intro_setup copies these four pages to $C000-$C3FF, and load_game copies $2F00-$2F30 to $0190, the code the loader runs after the load. Described in orientation.md and not annotated, as the kit does with loaders. Not all of it is the loader: from $2E70 there are runs of the GAME file's engine code, 31 bytes higher than in that file.
Code nothing calls, left in memory when the file was saved: long runs of it are the GAME file's engine code from $2FF7 to $37D3 there, 31 bytes lower, so another build of the engine.

Code nothing calls, after the title tune: left in memory when the file was saved, with runs that are the GAME file's engine code from $3CB4 to $3F1D there, 31 bytes lower, as at $3000-$37FF. Its first byte, $3C8C, is labelled: the title tune reads it.

The title's screen RAM: title_clear and title_2_clear clear it and the title draws on it (the Thalamus logo's layout, then the Creatures logo's colours from logo_screen, the credits from credits_screen and the lines written in later). The file's own bytes here are overwritten before they are seen.

Screen RAM while intro_setup runs ($D018 = $12), with every colour black, until title_start moves the screen to $4000. The bytes are left from the GAME file's screen: from $451D on they are that file's own at these addresses.
The Thalamus logo's live character set ($D018 = $02): title_clear zeroes it and logo_dissolve draws logo_chars into it. The file's own bytes here, cleared before use, are a copy of $5000-$57FF.
Zeros after logo_chars that nothing reads.
Left in memory from torture chamber 3's file, TI, when the file was saved: byte for byte that file's own at these addresses. Nothing reads them.
Left in memory from torture chamber 3's file, TI, when the file was saved: most of it is that file's own code at these addresses or a few bytes away. Nothing reads or runs it.
Bytes after logo_layout that nothing reads, left in memory when the file was saved: from $9D2D on they are torture chamber 3's file TI's own at these addresses.
The fast loader's copy at $C000, from $2C00-$2FFF (see there); the labels here come from intro_setup's copy loop and load_game's jump.
The KERNAL's vector table, not the game's: at reset its RESTOR routine reads the table through the ROM and the STA ($C3),Y at $FD27 writes the same 32 bytes into the RAM beneath (KERNAL 906145-02).
